items.fullText: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production November 8, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services. Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo . Apps to distract you from the endless cycle of doomscrolling
items.d: It's hard to break the cycle of doomscrolling, but there are plenty of apps that can help you spend more time on content that’s engaging and productive.
items.fullText: You open your phone to check the time or a quick message. The next thing you know, an hour has passed and you’ve scrolled through endless celebrity drama, cat videos, awful news stories, influencer rants, and whatever else the algorithm decided to throw at you. Even though you probably don’t want to keep wasting your time and energy on this mind-numbing content, you do it again the next day. Doomscrolling, the habit of spending excessive amounts of time consuming content on social media, has become incredibly widespread. A survey from last year found that 64% of Americans say they doomscroll . Researchers have warned that doomscrolling can negatively affect several aspects of your well-being, including your mental health and attention span. Spending long periods scrolling can lead to brain fatigue, difficulty focusing, and disrupted sleep. And if a lot of the content you’re consuming is negative or stressful, it can leave you feeling disheartened , anxious, and emotionally drained. It’s hard to break the cycle of doomscrolling, but there are plenty of apps that provide content that’s engaging and productive. Of course, you could always read a book or go for a walk (we have a guide on how to stop doomscrolling ), but this list is for when you have a few spare minutes and want something to do on your phone that isn’t endless scrolling. Finch Image Credits: Finch / Finch is a self-care pet app that’s designed to help you build healthy habits. You care for a cute virtual pet by completing small daily goals, such as drinking enough water, going on a walk, and practicing mindfulness. You can write about your day, complete a breathing exercise, or send good vibes to a friend by adding them to the app. The more self-care you do, the more your pet thrives. The app offers a fun way to trade mindless scrolling for small moments of self-care. Finch is available for free on iOS and Android . items.t: SNL has a new impression of Elon Musk, ‘the worst thing South Africa has ever done’
items.d: SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives.
items.fullText: Saturday Night Live cast member Jeremy Culhane unveiled his impression of Elon Musk last night, depicting the SpaceX and Tesla CEO as an awkward loser who fumbles his attempt to befriend the hosts of Weekend Update. This isn’t the first time the show has lampooned the world’s richest man ( and one-time SNL host ), with Mike Myers dropping by occasionally to wield a chainsaw before freezing and muttering, “Glitch!” Since Musk was in the news this week for spending half a billion dollars on candidates who lost in the midterms , then announcing plans to halt Cybertruck production , it’s maybe not surprising that Culhane’s version is a little less obnoxious and a little more desperate to be liked, doing his best to laugh off his setbacks and remind the audience, “ My car did a flip !” Eventually, Weekend Update co-host Colin Jost asks a pointed question about Musk’s week: “You moved to Texas because California was run by Democrats. You moved all your companies to Texas because you didn’t want to pay taxes. You even built your own town in Texas. And now Texas is run by Democrats. Now you’re going to have to pay taxes. So how does that make you feel?” Culhane nods along with each step of the question, then answers, “Bad?” To show that he’s a good sport about all this, Culhane also asks his chatbot Grok to do “an epic vulgar roast of me, Elon Musk.” Grok delivers, describing Musk as “the worst thing South Africa has ever done” and suggesting, “Maybe if you have 100 more kids, one of them will talk to you .” This week’s episode also featured a spoof of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” featuring Jane Wickline’s uncanny take on the Theranos founder (though most of the jokes focus on episode host Druski). SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives this season, starting with Wickline’s impression of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as a stuttering prophet of AI doom. items.t: Ninja’s AutoBarista is impressively versatile, but one feature was a dealbreaker for me
items.d: The AutoBarista's "Grind iQ" technology allows the machine to analyze your coffee beans to inform how it pulls a shot of espresso.
items.fullText: I’ve made about a dozen different kinds of coffee drinks with the Ninja AutoBarista , and I have absolutely no idea what sort of grind size, tamping pressure, water temperature, or extraction timing is necessary to pull espresso shots for any of those drinks. The AutoBarista takes care of these considerations for you, making it possible to brew 13 different drinks with just the press of a button. The AutoBarista seeks to create the experience of having a coffee shop inside of your home, but without having to master the complicated, time-consuming nuances of making perfect espresso. It makes drip coffee and espresso-and-milk drinks, like cappuccinos or flat white. The fully automatic espresso machine can even make a pretty fast cold brew or cold-pressed espresso (just add ice, or else it’s more like lukewarm brew). The AutoBarista’s versatility comes from its “ Grind iQ ” feature. This technology allows the machine to pick up on your coffee bean size, roast type, and freshness, auto-calibrating the grind size, weight, and dose of each brew to make your drink of choice. As you customize the number of shots in your drink, the intensity of the shot, and the temperature, Grind iQ adjusts as well. If using something like Grind iQ sounds like bowling with the bumpers up, or playing Mario Kart with steer assist, then this is not a machine for you — stick with your pour overs and enjoy your gooseneck electric kettle. This is not a machine for coffee snobs who want to control every last detail of the brewing process. Rather, it’s for people who love coffee, but have never analyzed their espresso pucks. November 6, 2026 by Soma Velayutham 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software , joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems. Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world. Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms. The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents. items.fullText: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents November 5, 2026 by Hannah Coutand 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power. What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt. Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity. The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU. Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests: Perplexity : Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system. items.fullText: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge November 5, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory. That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit. How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed. Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX. Agentic Inference Is Putting More Pressure on HBM Frontier models now have trillions of parameters — the values that hold what an AI model learned in training. KV cache, which holds the context the model needs to understand each active request without reprocessing the same information, is also expanding. items.fullText: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing. November 3, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.
